explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/828: 'Is it true that, for any a ∈ ℤ, there are infinitely many n such that φ(n) | n + a?' The Lean statement asserts ∀ a : ℤ, {n : ℕ | (φ n : ℤ) ∣ n + a} is infinite, with the divisibility in ℤ so negative a is handled correctly. Including n = 0 (φ(0) = 0) adds at most one element and does not affect infinitude. Faithful (positive form of the yes/no question).
